title: Beginner guide
sum: What Tallgrass is, your first hour and what each Gym badge unlocks.

blocks.x: Tallgrass is an idle Pokémon hunt that lives in the corner of your screen. Your trainer walks the route, your team of 4 battles every wild Pokémon on its own, and your **Catch rules** decide which ones get a ball. You make the big calls: who's on the team, what to catch, which island to hunt, when to fight the Gym.

title: FAQ
sum: Quick answers to the questions trainers ask most.

items: Why didn't my team catch that Pokémon?

Only what your [Catch rules](#wiki/rules) want gets a ball. By default: new species, Shiny, Void, Prismatic, perfect IVs and legendaries. Turn on "New looks", add it to the Catch list, or switch on "Catch everything".
Why did a Pokémon run away?

Ordinary wild Pokémon get 4 balls before the team finishes the battle, and from turn 7 they can flee. What your rules always want is never knocked out: it gets 40 balls (Catch list, legendaries) or 25 (other wants), Shiny/Void/Prismatic get every ball you have. Out of balls, it runs.
My Pokémon stopped levelling.
You hit the level cap: the next Gym's ace + 3 (21 / 31 / 41 / 51 / 61 / 71 / 81 / 91). Beat that Gym to raise it. Power-ups (Candy) still make it stronger. See [Levels & EXP](#wiki/exp).
A traded Pokémon dropped levels.
Pokémon above your level cap "shadow drop" to it. Their real level comes back step by step as your badges raise the cap, and they trade on at their real level.
What are my odds of breeding a Shiny, Void or Prismatic baby?

Use the [Breeding calculator](#wiki/daycare?at=h-breeding-calculator): pick both parents, their looks, your rank and Shiny Charm, and it shows the baby, the chance per egg of every look (all 8 combinations), Perfect IVs and Alpha, how many eggs for a 50% or 90% shot, and the hatch time with or without a nanny. Each parent with a look adds to its chance, and parents caught on different islands double the base odds.
How do I get legendaries?

Wild legendaries live on their island and wake once you've beaten that island's Gym **and** hold 3 badges. Raids are the steady source. Mythicals only come from [Raids](#wiki/raids). See [Legendaries & Mythicals](#wiki/legends).
How do I evolve Eevee (or any branching line)?

Branching lines never evolve on their own. When one reaches an evolution, the PC shows a green arrow: press Evolve and pick. Stones work from the Bag any time. Friendship evolutions (Espeon, Umbreon, Sylveon, Crobat…) open at Lv 20, or at any level once it's a **Good Buddy** (see [Buddy](#wiki/buddy)).
Can I stop my Pokémon from evolving?

Yes, in [Catch rules](#wiki/rules) → Evolving. Switch **Auto-evolve** off and nothing evolves on its own: Pokémon wait as "Ready to evolve" (green arrow in the PC) until you press Evolve. Or keep it on and turn on **Living dex**: your best copy of each species stays as it is, and extra copies still evolve. An {item:everstone|Everstone} stops one Pokémon.
How do I keep every copy of a species?
Add it to the **Never send** list (Catch rules → Never send → Species, or the lock on its Pokédex page). Auto-send and Send duplicates then skip every copy. See [the Professor](#wiki/professor).
How do trade evolutions work?
Trade it to a friend, or use a {item:linking_cord|Linking Cord} (Mart, $2,500).
Where do Master Balls come from?
See [Master Ball](#wiki/master): Raids (50,000+ damage), Gym Drake's badge, island checklists, the Stamp book, achievements and the rare legendary drop.
Does the game keep hunting while closed?
Yes, 3× slower than live, up to your Camping Gear cap (120 battles + 60 per level). Hidden to the tray it hunts at full speed. Bosses and Gyms wait for you.
What are Glimmer and Bounty Tickets?

Glimmer is the [Night Market](#wiki/market) currency (earned from your special finds). Bounty Tickets come from [Bounties](#wiki/bounties), the Tower, the Stamp book and raids, and buy [Style](#wiki/style) items and Game Corner capsules.
Can I lose a rare find?
A Shiny, Void, Prismatic or a new costume look is never knocked out by your team. If "Battle rare finds myself" is on, it waits 2 minutes for you. Out of balls, it runs, so keep auto-restock on.
Why can't I sell on the Night Market yet?

New trainers can buy right away, but selling opens **2 days after you start playing online**. Once you're selling, you can change a listing's price without taking it down (see [Night Market](#wiki/market)).
My panels moved after an update.
From v0.54 your panel layout and monitor settings are also kept in your save folder, so they stay put through updates. If one is ever lost, the game brings it back from there.
Do I have to pay for anything?
No. Tallgrass is free and nothing is behind a paywall. If you want to follow its development, Settings → Help → **Support** opens the Patreon page.
Is Tallgrass official?
No. It is a free fan-made game, not affiliated with Nintendo, Game Freak, Creatures or The Pokémon Company.

title: Mega Evolution & forms
sum: 111 battle forms: Megas, Primal, Origin, Crowned, Ultra Necrozma and fusions, plus regional forms.

blocks.x: Mega Evolution in battle

Give a Pokémon its Mega Stone (or orb, Rusted item…) from the PC. It fights in its normal form and **charges up**: +1 each turn it's out, +1 more if it was hit. At 3 charge it Mega Evolves for the rest of that battle, keeping its HP, status and stat changes. One Mega per battle, like the games. Primal Reversion (Red/Blue Orb), Origin Forme, the Crowned forms and Ultra Burst work the same way. Holding the stone, a Buddy is always shown in that form.
Which Pokémon can Mega Evolve

A Pokémon that can change form holding an item has a **Mega** chip with its stone on its card, on the Hunt cards and in its PC slot tooltip, and the PC filter **Can Mega Evolve** finds them all. An earlier stage says which evolution can (Charmander: "its evolution Charizard can"). Primal Reversion, Origin Forme, Crowned and Ultra Burst are named as such; fusions have their own box on the Evolution tab. 95 species can:

blocks.label: Can Mega Evolve or change form (95)

blocks.x: Getting Mega Stones

items: Beaten wild Pokémon of a Mega line drop their stone 4% of the time.
A wild Pokémon with a Mega form Mega Evolves for the fight 6% of the time (legendaries and Mythicals 10%); then its stone **always** drops, caught or beaten.
Mega and Mega Alpha [bosses](#wiki/bosses) always drop their stone.
The Mart buys Mega Stones for $2,000 (a legendary's or Mythical's item for $5,000).

blocks.x: Fusions

Kyurem (with Reshiram or Zekrom), Calyrex (with Glastrier or Spectrier) and Necrozma (with Solgaleo or Lunala) fuse in the PC from their Evolution tab. Nothing is used up. The fusion shows **every special look of the two** (a Prismatic Reshiram + a normal Kyurem = a Prismatic White Kyurem) with those looks' boosts; level, IVs, Power, held item and nickname are the base Pokémon's. Splitting gives both back exactly as they were. Dusk Mane and Dawn Wings Necrozma can then Ultra Burst holding Ultranecrozium Z.
Regional forms

Alolan, Galarian, Hisuian and Paldean forms are their own species with the base's Pokédex number. They live in the wild like any other Pokémon; an evolution into a regional form (Pikachu → Alolan Raichu) only happens in the wild, never by evolving.

title: How the hunt works
sum: Encounters, the stack, Rush, playing while away and specials that wait for you.

blocks.x: Wild Pokémon stack up in the grass on a clock: one every **14 s**, ×0.95 per Sweet Scent level, never faster than 6 s. Your party fights them one at a time; the count up top is the stack. While the game is open the stack holds up to 60 + 60 per Camping Gear level.
While you're away

items: Closed, your team keeps hunting **3× slower** than live, up to **120 battles + 60 per Camping Gear level** (120–1,020).
Hidden to the tray, it hunts at full speed. Bosses and Gyms wait until you're back.
Every battle is a real one: catches follow your Catch rules, HP and Pokémon Center trips line up, eggs warm.
A "What you missed" recap greets you when you come back.

blocks.x: Rush

From your first badge, **Rush** clears the stack at once: up to 25 encounters per charge. You hold up to 2 charges and get one back every 45 minutes. After being away, a free Rush clears up to 30 of what stacked.
Specials wait for you

Shiny, Void, Prismatic finds, new costume looks and prize encounters ring a bell and wait **2 minutes** for you to battle them yourself (Settings → Battle rare finds myself). In your own battle you pick the moves and throw any ball, including the special balls. If you don't come, the team handles it with your rules. You can also ring the Pokédex bell on any species so it always waits, and set Legendaries or island bosses to "Call me first".
HP between battles

items: HP carries from battle to battle and comes back at 15% of max HP a minute.
A Pokémon that faints sits out 45 s and returns at 50% HP.
If the whole party goes down, it rests at the Pokémon Center for 60 s and comes back fully healed.
A **double KO** (the foe and your last Pokémon faint on the same turn) still counts as a win, and your team goes to the Pokémon Center too ("Your whole party fainted too!").

blocks.x: Daily gift

Once a UTC day the Poké Mart leaves 10 Poké Balls in your Bag (+5 Great Balls from the Bug Catcher rank), with a 30% chance of 5 more Great Balls and 30% of a Rare Candy. Out of balls and under $20? Professor Glow sends 10 Poké Balls (every 5 minutes at most).

title: Catching
sum: The catch formula, a catch calculator, and how auto battles decide when to throw.

blocks.x: The formula
Each ball's chance = (catch rate (+ Heavy Ball) × ball × HP factor × status ÷ 255) × look × legendary × Catching Charm, capped at **95%** (a Master Ball always works).

items: HP factor
1 − ⅔ × HP left (full HP ×0.33, 1 HP ≈ ×1)
Status
Asleep or frozen ×2.5, other status ×1.5
Look
Void ×0.6, Prismatic ×0.4, Void Prismatic ×0.3 (Shiny: ×1)
Legendary
Catching Charm
+4% per level (up to +100%)

blocks.x: In auto battles

items: Only Pokémon your Catch rules want get a ball. The team picks the ball: a Master Ball if your Master Ball rule allows it, else the ball you picked in Catch rules, else Ultra → Great → Poké for specials and the cheapest first for the rest.
A **Catcher** (a Pokémon knowing False Swipe, Hold Back, a sleep or paralysis move, or Nuzzle) steps in from the bench, puts it to sleep or paralyses it, and False Swipes it to 1 HP before throwing.
**Break** Pokémon on the bench lower its guard every 2 turns (up to 3 times): each time +8% catch chance × their role strength (Wide Lens ×1.5). In auto battles the total is capped at 97%.

Shiny, Void, Prismatic, new costume looks and prize encounters get **every ball you have** and are never knocked out. Anything else your rules always want (new species, Catch list, perfect IVs, legendaries) is never knocked out either and gets 40 balls (Catch list, legendaries) or 25 (the rest), then runs.
"Catch everything" Pokémon get 4 balls, and from turn 7 a missed throw can make them flee (stronger species and lower levels than yours flee less).
Prize encounters can't be missed: out of balls, Professor Glow sends 5 Great Balls on the spot, and if one gets away it comes back as your next encounter.

IVs are 0–31 for each stat, fixed by the Pokémon's personality. The card shows their average as a %: **perfect** 100%, **great** 80%+, **good** 55%+. Perfect-IV Pokémon have all six at 31. Natures raise one stat ×1.1 and lower another ×0.9 (5 are neutral). title: Day Care & eggs
sum: Breeding calculator, pens, egg timing, look odds, IVs, the Hearth and the Nanny.

blocks.x: Breeding calculator

Pick two parents and their looks: see the baby, its chance per egg of every look (all 8 combinations, with previews), Perfect IVs and Alpha, how many eggs you need for a good shot, and how long eggs take with and without a nanny. The maths is the game's own, checked against it on every wiki update.
Pens and pairs

Each breeding pen holds two Pokémon from your PC. With every wild encounter they gain a little EXP, and if they get along they lay eggs. You start with one pen; more open with badges (pen 1: start, pen 2: 2 badges, pen 3: 4 badges, pen 4: 6 badges).

An egg needs 100 progress (one per encounter, two for a same-family pair). The baby is the **first form** of the non-Ditto parent's line. Eggs then hatch after a number of encounters by rarity: Common 40, Uncommon 60, Rare 90, Legendary 120.
Egg looks and IVs

items: Base odds = your wild Shiny odds × 2 ÷ 3 (eggs are better than the wild), **halved** when the parents were caught on different islands.
Each parent with a look adds a bonus chance: Shiny 1 in 128, Void 1 in 384, Prismatic 1 in 1,024 per parent.
Perfect IVs: the rank's odds + 1 in 48 per perfect parent, ×3 with a {item:destiny_knot|Destiny Knot}, which also gives the baby the best of 3 IV rolls.
Alpha: 1 in 64 per Alpha parent.

blocks.x: **Comparing parents**: a pen shows both parents' six IVs side by side: green = higher than the other parent, red = lower, gold = a perfect 31, with the nature's raised and lowered stats marked. Right-click a parent to open its full card.
The table is the Shiny chance per egg; Void and Prismatic follow the same rules at ×3 and ×8 rarer bases.
The basket

Eggs wait in your basket: 6 / 7 / 8 / 9 / 10 / 11 / 12 / 14 / 16 / 18 / 20 eggs for Egg Basket upgrade levels 0–10, plus 2 per Basket lantern from the Glimmer Shop (up to 6). A full basket of ready eggs stops new ones. While you're away (closed, hidden, or 10 minutes without input), laying pauses at 25 waiting eggs + lanterns. Raid, gift, costume and prize eggs never take a basket slot.
The Hearth
One Pokémon sits by the basket and warms the eggs without taking a squad slot. Eggs warm at the best of the Hearth and your party: any Fire type ×1.5, Flame Body / Magma Armor / Steam Engine ×2.
The Nanny

An egg nanny sits in its own Day Care slot and hatches ready eggs for you: one every **10 minutes** of hunting for Happiny, Chansey, Togepi, Togetic; one every **5 minutes** of hunting for Blissey, Togekiss. Away battles count too, and its babies wait quietly for their reveal.

A special nanny is faster: **Shiny 10%**, **Void 15%**, **Prismatic 20%** less time per egg (its best look counts; a Prismatic Blissey hatches one every 4 minutes). Only the hatch time changes: what hatches and its odds stay the same. The Nanny seat shows the cut and the minutes.
Babies can't level or evolve until their hatch reveal plays. Branching lines (Eevee…) never evolve on their own: you pick.
